# Workload Report for DSH
> **See your effort and your token spend on the same picture** — by **date** and by **workspace**: a
calendar heatmap, time-of-day analysis, workspace share, model usage, and a **one-click self-contai

ned HTML report** you can send straight to a client.
> A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin. Current vers

** you can send straight to a client.
> A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin. Current version: **2.5.0**.
中文 · 日本語 · Deutsch · Français · Español · Русский · Português · English
## What it is
DSH shows stats for the **current session**. This plugin adds the cross-session, cross-project, cros
s-time view: which dates and which workspaces your effort went to, which hours you were productive,
which models consumed the tokens, and what it cost — plus a static report for clients, teammates or
sumed the tokens, and what it cost — plus a static report for clients, teammates or monthly reviews.
**Not only cost, but the work behind it.** Active time, active days and turns show what you actually
did; tokens and estimated cost show what it consumed. Numbers use the same definitions everywhere,
so the dashboard and the exported report agree.
## Features (2.0.0)
- **Nine KPIs (two rows)**: cumulative active time (**net active**, waiting shown on a second line),
total tokens (full integer you can verify), model-time share, active days, **conversations / turns*
* (one merged card, **steps no longer shown**), **output speed tok/s** (subtitle = TTFT), average ou

tput per request, cache-read share, and the most active model.
- **Daily usage trend**: calendar hea
tmap (Mon–Sun × Year-Week, colour and bar height = active time) or a bar chart; weekends use a diffe
rent colour, the peak bar is always labelled, and every calendar cell, bar, weekday total and axis l

abel has its own tooltip.
- **Time of day**: bars default to **token output** (switchable to **turns
**); the dots above the bars show **human-message density**. Peak bars are highlighted and labelled;

the legend sits on one row.
- **Workspace share**: Top 6 + others donut, switchable between **time*

* and **tokens**.
- **Model token share**: a compact donut on the dashboard; full model details live

in the next tab.
- **Model usage tab**: treemap (area = token share, Top 8 + others), stacked daily
trend (Top 6 models), a detail table (**speed tok/s / TTFT / provider** / share / requests / input
/ output / cache read / cache-hit rate / estimated cost — 11 columns, with ratio bars on speed and r
equests), metric chips (Token / requests / model time), click-to-filter, and official pricing links.

Costs are estimated only for models with official public prices.
- **Top sessions and daily detail*
*: ratio bars in the main numeric columns (sessions: turns / steps / active / output; daily detail:
conversations / turns / active / tokens) and sortable headers on the sessions table. The daily detai
l table is **expanded by default**, covers the last 31 days, and **paginates at 10 days per page** (

no pager unless there is more than one page).

## Privacy
All statistics stay on your machine. The plugin registers **read-only** HTTP routes only: by default
no outbound requests, no telemetry, no user content collected. It writes only its own index cache p
lus the optional AI-profile cache; nothing else in your harness data is touched. The exported report
may contain session titles unless you pass `anonymize=1`.
**Optional balance chip — off by default.** Only when you set `balance.enabled: true` does the host
call the official `deepseekAccount` service: `getBalance()` makes the **host** request `https://plat
form.deepseek.com/api/v0/users/get_user_summary` (the account balance endpoint). It is opt-in and ca
ched for `balance.refreshMs`. The top-up/usage links come from the service's local `getState()` and
need no network. A failed or timed-out query shows an em dash with a top-up link — never an error di
alog. The balance is rendered only in your own toolbar chip and is **never written into the exported
ce is rendered only in your own toolbar chip and is **never written into the exported HTML report**.
**AI user profile — included by default, manual trigger only.** Opening the panel / `probe` only rea
ds enabled, sign-in state, and provider/model; it **never calls a model**. Only after you click **Ge
nerate profile** does the plugin call the `llm` service (and your configured model provider) with th
e aggregate whitelist described in AI user profile, always using a window of at least 30 days. No co
nversation text, titles, paths, session ids, or event logs are sent. The response is cached on disk
in the plugin's own directory; the static HTML report never contains it. If the service is missing,
you are not signed in, the call times out, or parsing fails, the card falls back to local rules and
shows the reason — no error dialog. This side call is not included in the plugin's token / cost repo
rt. Set `aiProfile.enabled: false` to hide the entry and guarantee zero model calls.
## Compatibility
- DSH `0.2.x`, **including `alpha` prereleases** (developed and verified against `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0
.2.1-alpha.2` and `0.2.2-rc.1`). The manifest declares `engines.dsh >= 0.2.1-alpha.0` with **no uppe
r bound**, so upgrading DSH to a newer 0.x build does not exclude the plugin by version range; newer
versions are allowed to load but only the versions above are explicitly verified. The plugin depend
s only on official interfaces (`sessionProjections` / `sessionProjectionCache` / `sessionQuery`) and

Node built-ins, never on internal file formats.
- The first launch cold-reads historical sessions w
hose projection checkpoints are missing; the API returns progressively filled data with `indexing: t

rue`, and restarts reuse the persisted index.
- Very early **v0-format sessions** may not be migrata
ble/readable by the current harness. They are excluded from statistics and the UI reports how many.
